setup: The claim is that \(f(n) = n^2 + n + [[c]]\) is prime for every positive integer \(n\).

steps.say: A single \(n\) with a composite value refutes the claim, so the task is to find the smallest such \(n\) rather than to argue about all of them.
Testing in order, \(f(n)\) is prime for every \(n\) from 0 to [[last_prime]], so no smaller positive \(n\) refutes the claim.
At \(n = [[n]]\) the value is \([[value]]\), and [[value]] = [[factor1]] \cdot [[factor2]], so it is not prime.
